result_summary.result:
Investigation complete. Here's what I found and what I recommend.

## TL;DR

Recommend having the devboard **server parse `WORK.md` directly from the worklog mount it already has**, expose the backlog sections in `/api/tasks`, and render them as lightweight collapsed rows — not as task cards, and not by having the worklog CLI write stub task files. Everything needed is already in place: the mount, the SSE change-watcher, a blessed precedent for re-parsing a worklog-owned file in Python, and a `Repo:` field on tickets for grouping.

## Why the gap exists

A devboard task file is only ever created by `worklog start` (`OnStart` in `worklog/internal/devboard/devboard.go:392`) — it's explicitly "disposable live telemetry" for in-flight work, with worklog as the system of record (`devboard/schema.md`). Tickets in `## Next` and `## Someday` exist only as blocks in `WORK.md`, so `server.py`'s scan of `<data-root>/<repo>/*.yaml` never sees them. The same blindness covers a `## Now`/`## Waiting` ticket whose task file is missing (started while the devboard dir didn't exist, or untracked via `worklog task untrack`) — worth fixing in the same stroke.

## What makes the read-side fix cheap

- **The data is already mounted.** `server.py` reads `notes/<id>.md` and `FEEDBACK.md` from `WORKLOG_DIR` (read-only); `WORK.md` sits at the root of that same mount. No new mount, no new write path, and the "rendered, never copied" rule is preserved.
- **There's an explicit precedent for a second parser.** The container ships no `worklog` binary, so `server.py` already re-implements the FEEDBACK.md parser (`_parse_feedback`, `server.py:125`), permissively, pinned by `test_server.py`, with the README documenting that the two sides extend independently. A WORK.md reader follows the identical pattern, and the needed subset is small and stable: `## Section` headings, `- [ ] **ID** — Title` bullet lines, and indented `**Field**:` metadata (see the three regexes at `worklog/internal/parse/work.go:17-21`). You only need `id`, `title`, `section`, `repo`, `type`, `tags`, `parent` — skip unknown fields like the feedback reader does.
- **Hot-reload is one line.** Add a `WORK.md` stat to `_snapshot()` (`server.py:43`) next to the existing `FEEDBACK.md` stat, and section moves ripple to the browser over the existing SSE stream within ~2s.
- **Tickets carry a repo hint.** `worklog add` has an optional `--repo`/form field mirrored into the block's `**Repo**:` metadata, and the convention (git-repo basename) matches devboard's grouping-directory names from `RepoName()`. So most backlog rows can be attached to the right repo group; repo-less ones need a fallback.

## Recommended design

**API**: add a `backlog` key to `/api/tasks` carrying every parsed `WORK.md` block — `{id, title, section, state, repo, type, tags, parent, started}` — in document order (WORK.md order within a section is the priority order; the line-oriented parse preserves it). Ship all sections, not just Next/Someday, and let the **frontend do the join**: it already holds every task card (including archived), so it can subtract blocks whose id matches some card's `worklog:` field. That keeps the Python parser dumb and automatically makes an un-mirrored Now/Waiting ticket visible with a "no task file" hint. A ticket disappearing from the backlog panel and appearing as a card the moment `worklog start` runs falls out for free — no lifecycle code.

**Frontend**: render backlog rows in the existing `bandfold`/`fold` idiom (`index.html:448`), collapsed by default like `Friction · N` and `Archived · N` — these are not cards; they have no plan/scorecard/phase and shouldn't inflate the grid or stats. Two reasonable placements: a row-strip per repo group (`Queued · N`, Next before Someday, with a section chip), plus a global fold for rows whose `Repo:` is empty or matches no group. I'd lean per-repo with a global "unassigned" fold, mirroring how the ticket data actually distributes.

**What to exclude**: epic children never get WORK.md blocks in Next/Someday (`add.go:45` — `WorkMD` is "empty for child"); pending children already render on the epic card's `children[]` roster, so there's no double-listing hazard as long as you only render top-level blocks. `## Waiting` tickets were necessarily started, so the join will almost always subtract them.

**Tests**: extend `test_server.py` to pin the WORK.md reader the way it pins the feedback reader — including the malformed-file case (a bad `WORK.md` should mean "no backlog panel", never a broken page, same contract as feedback).

## Alternatives considered

- **Worklog writes stub task files for backlog tickets** (`worklog add` → YAML with a `queued` marker): rejected. It inverts the schema's ownership philosophy — task files are disposable telemetry, worklog the record — and buys a pile of lifecycle machinery: create/delete/reorder syncing, section moves, back-fill when the devboard dir is created later, and permanent desync whenever the human edits `WORK.md` by hand (a supported workflow). It would also blur the "a task file means started work" invariant the archive/stats/attention UI leans on.
- **Ship the `worklog` binary in the container and shell out to `status`/JSON**: rejected — couples the Python image to the Go build; the README documents no-binary-in-container as a deliberate choice with the dual-parser pattern as the sanctioned answer.
- **Go side writes a derived `backlog.json` into the devboard data dir on every mutation**: avoids the Python parser, but re-imports the staleness problem (hand-edits to WORK.md desync until the next CLI run) and needs a hook on every mutating command — while the live file is already sitting on the mount.

## Caveats

- The Python/Go parser duplication is real drift risk; mitigate by parsing only the minimal field subset, skipping unknowns, and pinning with tests — the same bet FEEDBACK.md already makes, and the WORK.md block grammar has a validator (`worklog validate`) keeping it disciplined on the Go side.
- `Repo:` is optional and free-text, so the repo join is best-effort; the unassigned fold is the honest fallback rather than guessing.
- The `_parse_task` guard style (`"/" not in wl`) should be applied consistently if any backlog field is ever used to build a path — for the recommended design nothing is, since backlog rows are display-only.
